pillar_reactions.evidence: Delivered as form-first, light-to-heavy, mobility as the foundation: 'the first month is always about mastering the form... no matter how experienced the individual is'. The prospect tied it straight to his own experience and then argued the case for the rep: 'we've had kettlebell classes and people are going and all over... Especially when there's things like snatches', 'that would be where I would need that assistance', and unprompted at the end, 'the people that I know that work out with the kettlebell, of which there are very few at the gym, are the ones that have the best looking bodies.'

The rep pitched eating for health and micronutrients over 'chicken, rice, and broccoli eight times a day'. The prospect agreed it matched his prescribed diet, and then took over the topic and taught the rep — plant diversity for the microbiome ('try new vegetable, radish, daikon, because those have fibers that the new bacteria use in order to sustain and grow') and fermented foods. The rep asked one good question ('Can you eat fermented veg?') and otherwise followed. Understood and agreed, but the pillar had no persuasive work left to do: this prospect is already more nutritionally literate than the pitch.

Never delivered. No weekly check-ins, no 24/7 coach access, no chasing on missed workouts or nutrition, no form-video review loop. The rep described tailoring and named Trevor as the coach, but the accountability pillar itself was skipped entirely — notable because this prospect's actual gap is that his structure disappeared when the gym classes stopped, and accountability is the pillar that answers it.

anchors.raw: they want you to gradually start in, you know, go from body weight squats to, uh, goblet squats with maybe 12 pounds on an incline board, or then in, after two or three weeks at 12, go to 18 pounds and see how you're doing
anchors.note: The strongest anchor on the call and the one the rep never addressed. He already has a free, personalised, progressive loading protocol from three doctors, complete with a tolerance marker and a return-to-full-intensity timeline ('for two or three weeks, go up to like 70% of what you could do before. And then after like a month, then you're fine'). That is precisely the tailored-progression value the programme sells. The programme's actual differentiator against it is technique coaching and accountability — the one the rep argued well and the one he never mentioned.

anchors.raw: someone like myself, what would you, what weight, if I was to go buy one or two, just to get, you know, probably good, what are we talking, 12 pounds, 18 pounds, 24 pounds?
anchors.note: The prospect is assembling the do-it-yourself version live on the call — he is already a gym member, has two acres to train on, and is now sourcing his own bells. The rep answered with specific recommendations ('215, 224') and gave away the entry consult for free, leaving the prospect equipped to start alone in five weeks with no reason to come back.

anchors.raw: the people that I know that work out with the kettlebell, of which there are very few at the gym, are the ones that have the best looking bodies. The people who lumber around on the deadlift... they don't ever look any different than they did 10 years ago.
anchors.note: Volunteered unprompted in the closing minutes. The modality is fully sold — there is no unfamiliar-modality resistance here at all. Whatever eventually blocks or converts this deal, it will not be belief in kettlebells.

unmet_demand.want: Coaching that starts now, at the bottom of a medically supervised rehabilitation ramp, and progresses in step with gut-recovery markers over the three-to-six-month window
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep judged the programme could not be used yet and said so directly — 'I also don't want you to pay for something that you can't use right now' — and gated enrolment behind the prospect proving himself in a gym first. The offer as it exists starts at a level of readiness this prospect will not reach for a month or more, so the rehabilitation window itself is unserved.

unmet_demand.want: Technique coaching on snatches and swings specifically, which he named as the one thing he cannot self-teach
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme does do this — form mastery in month one with video review is the core of it — and the rep described the form-first principle, but never connected it back to the prospect's own stated need or offered any way to access it inside the deferral window.
